Diagnosis.Cancer Type: adenocarcinoma of the head of the pancreas

Additional Comments: The patient, a 69-year-old African-American woman, has been experiencing increased fatigue, nausea, emesis, and burping over the past three weeks. She has also reported a one-week history of bilateral lower extremity edema, which improves with leg elevation, and a recent onset of dark-colored urine for three days. Despite a poor appetite, she has gained some weight. Her upper abdominal pain is managed with Methadone BID and Oxycodone PRN. She continues to take Creon with meals and snacks. Recent imaging indicates an increase in the size of the pancreatic mass, resulting in biliary obstruction and proximal intrahepatic and extrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation, as well as increased pancreatic ductal dilatation and partial obstruction of the duodenum. An urgent referral to GI for an ERCP has been placed, and lower extremity ultrasound did not identify any DVTs.
